references.text: David expresses joy over God's word as a treasure, similar to the joy the man in the parable feels when he finds the treasure.
God gives treasures in darkness to Cyrus, which can be seen as a metaphor for the value of God's kingdom that is hidden and then found.
Jesus encourages gathering treasures in heaven, which resonates with the image of the kingdom of heaven as a treasure.
Jesus tells the rich young man to sell what he has and give to the poor to have a treasure in heaven, parallel to selling everything for the treasure of the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus encourages selling what one has and giving alms to have an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, similar to the action of the man in the parable.
The first Christians sold their property and possessions and shared everything they had, reflecting the idea of giving up earthly goods for heavenly values.
Moses considered Christ's disgrace a greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, because he looked forward to the reward, parallel to valuing the kingdom of heaven above all else.
